First release: Raft consensus and a replicated key-value store, tested by a deterministic simulator and by a chaos test of real processes.

**Consensus:** elections, log replication with conflict hints, the current-term commit rule, PreVote, CheckQuorum, ReadIndex reads, snapshots with InstallSnapshot.

**Server:** a CRC'd write-ahead log with fsync and torn-tail repair, atomic snapshot files, an HTTP transport with an optional HMAC cluster secret, a client API with `307` redirects to the leader and exactly-once writes, `/status` and Prometheus `/metrics`.

**Testing:**
- Simulator: 200 consensus and 100 key-value seeds per mode on every push, in three modes (everything on, classic, bare), plus 2,000 and 300 fresh seeds per mode in CI. Zero violations.
- Seven controls (broken builds) that the checks must catch; `TestControlMatrix` shows no single mode catches all seven.
- Chaos: three processes, `kill -9` and `SIGSTOP` of the leader for 60 s under five clients, checked with Porcupine. One run: 8,979 operations, 15 kills, 13 freezes, no violations; the stale-read control is caught.

Write-up: [Every feature I added to my Raft hid a bug from my tests](https://kage7047.github.io/writing/features-hide-bugs/)

Verify a download: `gh attestation verify faultline_v0.1.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz --repo Kage7047/faultline`
